note: Reference architecture for a multi-account, environment-isolated ML platform with registry-driven promotion and human-in-the-loop sign-off, extended to LLM adapter versioning. Built for regulated industries.

Diagnosing GPU cluster failures that single-node debugging never teaches — NCCL timeouts that are really storage, DataLoader forks hanging collectives, GPUs that pass health checks and corrupt results. You leave with a failure-signature runbook.

The best pure-craft session in the catalog for your role: profile kernels, tune collectives, read EFA and Lustre counters, build the dashboards yourself, and leave with a goodput methodology. Full-day-caliber depth.

Build a working continuous evaluation pipeline: evaluation datasets, LLM-as-judge plus programmatic scoring, performance tracking over time, alerts on quality regressions. You leave with something you can adapt Monday.

A live decision framework for SFT vs DPO vs RLAIF vs RLVR vs multi-turn RL, mapped onto SageMaker Serverless, Training Jobs, HyperPod, and Bedrock Custom Model Import. Bring a real use case; they place it on the map.

The full governed path: managed MLflow, SageMaker Pipelines with lineage, Model Registry with model cards and approval gates, CI/CD promotion, drift monitoring. Approval gates and lineage are exactly what an ATO package asks for.

The synthetic-data flywheel for robotics and AV: generate rare edge cases, post-train policies, evaluate, repeat, on HyperPod with EKS and heterogeneous GPU pools. This is the robotics-plus-ML-infra intersection you care about.

Strands Robots SDK: one Robot() call gives an agent hands, MuJoCo by default and real hardware with a parameter change. Covers perception, VLA policies (GR00T, Cosmos 3, LeRobot), edge-to-cloud split, fleet mesh, and sim-to-real.
Building data products good enough for agents to consume. The upstream work that determines whether any of your downstream agent work succeeds.
A decision framework for choosing compute across HPC and AI at scale by price and timing. The session that saves you the most money per minute spent in it.
Hands-on build of production clusters with AWS Parallel Computing Service — job submission, resource optimization, the managed replacement for hand-rolled ParallelCluster.

Whiteboards the whole physical-AI pipeline and compares EKS vs Batch vs ParallelCluster across simulation, training, evaluation, and edge deployment, with Capacity Blocks and Spot for cost. They solve attendee architectures live — bring yours.
What power users actually do to keep multi-agent orchestration from going brittle as context fills and the agent loses its plan. Bring your own edge cases.

Reusable skills that encode team know-how, custom agents for specific jobs, and steering files that carry conventions across sessions. Demoed in Kiro but the principles transfer to any agentic coding tool.
The single most useful hour if you ship into Government Regions. Real ATO strategies, service parity gaps, and deployment patterns for Bedrock agents across classification levels.

Build a digital twin of a multi-robot manufacturing cell in 60 minutes — virtual PLCs, real fieldbus, Omniverse physics, EC2 backing it. You leave with a validated robotic program and a reusable blueprint.
NIST 800-171 / CMMC L2 landing zone deep dive, including what they got wrong and iterated on. Open-source CloudFormation on GitHub — a reusable asset, not just a talk.
Agentic orchestration inside high-side environments under IL4/IL5 and zero trust. Rare to get this level of detail on the constrained side of the fence.

Provable safety envelopes for probabilistic agents, drawn from the formal verification research behind AgentCore policy — automated reasoning for policy correctness, action-space reduction before execution. This is how you get an agent past a security review.

Distinguished-level: head-of-line blocking on prefill, decode stragglers, pipeline bubbles, temporally-disaggregated pipeline parallelism, constrained decoding with context-sensitive grammars, KV-cache parallelism for multi-million contexts.
What neurosymbolic AI can actually prove about agent behavior: autoformalization into temporal logic, SAT solvers, LLM-guided proof search in Lean, and an honest map of what remains undecidable.

Distinguished-level failure analysis of a trajectory-conditioned lidar world model for a hospital robot fleet: why standard losses fail for generative spatial prediction, why rotation breaks factored attention. A diagnostic framework, not a product pitch.
Fine-tune a transformer world model and deploy robotic agents for real-time inference on Trainium, with parameter-efficient training strategies.
Full-stack LLM serving on Trainium: vLLM Neuron, disaggregated inference, prefix-cache-aware routing, then EKS topology-aware scheduling and fault recovery underneath.
RLHF and GRPO on Trainium via Neuron, TorchTitan, TRL, and vLLM, with a co-located vs disaggregated RL architecture comparison.
Governance for agents making high-stakes decisions — a workshop, so you build the controls rather than hear about them.
Vision-language model training that survives node crashes and corrupt checkpoints. You simulate failures and recover. Directly relevant if you touch multimodal or geospatial models.
Managed multi-turn RL on SageMaker that wraps a Strands, LangChain, or CrewAI agent in under 10 lines — reward design, rollouts in managed gym environments, decoupled training compute.
Distributed training on Trainium through native PyTorch and TorchTitan — cluster setup, parallelism strategies, tuning. The cleanest hands-on route into Trainium if you have never touched Neuron.
You run both unified and disaggregated inference architectures yourself, move KV cache over EFA, and benchmark against agentic traffic. Leaves you with a real decision framework and runnable configs.
Panel on world models across video, vision, language, and action for physical AI and autonomous systems, with researchers and customers on production deployments.

A Strands agent running the entire RL loop autonomously: generates reward functions from a natural-language objective, evaluates in simulation, diagnoses failures, tunes hyperparameters, iterates to convergence.
End-to-end data prep, distributed training, and serving on HyperPod, including simulating a node failure and watching training auto-resume. Tiered checkpointing and managed KV cache.
Running coding agents at scale on AgentCore — the infrastructure question once agents stop being one developer's laptop experiment.

HyperPod as one shared GPU pool across data prep, training, post-training, and inference, with team isolation and submission strategies. The multi-team utilization problem, which is a real one in an agency.
Dataset prep as a first-class stage — profiling, auto-labeling, human review of edge cases, dedup, toxicity filtering, synthetic data for coverage gaps, then formatting for SFT, DPO, RLVR, and RLAIF.
On-policy distillation on HyperPod EKS: compress a large teacher into a domain-specialized student using the student's own rollouts. Cheaper and more stable than RLVR, and no verifier needed.
One HyperPod training pipeline that deploys the same model into Bedrock or AgentCore, with governance following the model rather than bolted on afterward.
A fine-tuning pipeline that proves its own results: baseline eval, QLoRA fine-tune, RLAIF/RLVR pass, re-eval against the same bar. The discipline most fine-tuning work skips.

Full NVIDIA-plus-AWS physical AI pipeline in one workshop: Isaac Sim synthetic data, GR00T and Cosmos training, Omniverse twin, Greengrass edge deploy, AgentCore fleet orchestration. Sponsored, but the toolchain coverage is unmatched.
Open lakehouse on Apache Iceberg for analytics and AI. The format decision that keeps your data portable across engines and, importantly, across partitions.
From prompt to pipeline: the chalk-talk version of agentic data engineering, with more room to argue about where it breaks.
Agentic data engineering inside SageMaker — agents building and maintaining pipelines rather than you writing every ETL job.
Governing agents with data quality, lineage, and business context. Lineage is the artifact auditors actually ask you for.
Specs, not vibes: strangling a monolith from inside the IDE. The disciplined counterweight to vibe-coding, which matters more when your code needs to pass review.
Migrating existing HPC estates onto PCS at scale. Relevant if you inherit an on-prem cluster, which in public sector you usually do.

DCV streaming an Omniverse and Isaac Sim workstation from EC2 G instances to a browser, with AWS Batch running the same scenes headless across GPU fleets. Fixes the 'engineers lack RTX hardware' problem directly.
Using AI to tune HPC configurations on AWS rather than hand-tuning them.
AWS Batch orchestrating burst simulation and GPU training end to end, with outputs flowing through a shared data lake back into training. Solves the no-standing-fleet budget problem.
How Kiro validates specs before writing any code. Directly relevant to shipping under a compliance regime where intent has to be documented anyway.
Compares Dedicated Local Zones, Outposts, and Regions against data residency, key management, and network separation — plus detecting non-permitted data flows. The sovereignty decision matrix.
California Community Colleges cut attempted financial-aid fraud 64% with SageMaker. A genuine public-sector ML case study with numbers, not a genAI demo.

Commanding autonomous drone fleets for search-and-rescue with Bedrock Agents, Greengrass, and SageMaker, escalating to humans on confidence thresholds. Human-machine teaming with a public-safety mission.
Hands-on CDK build of an edge-to-cloud tokenization data plane: sensitive data stays local, masked payloads go to Bedrock. The workaround pattern for data-localization mandates.

Zero-shot forecasting with Chronos 2 in SageMaker Unified Studio — no historical training, no cold-start problem. Framed for retail, but the pattern transfers to caseload, demand, and staffing forecasts.
Air Force SOC + AWS built a multi-agent Bedrock system for log analysis and one-click containment across DoD accounts. Fifteen minutes, high signal.
Kiro in a regulated federal context — steering rules to constrain agent behavior, hooks for automated testing and docs. Practical if compliance is what slows your team down.
Evaluating AI safety with formal guarantees rather than benchmark scores. Pairs with INV506 and INV526 as a coherent three-session arc.
How neurosymbolic AI formalizes natural language into verifiable logic — the mechanism underneath IND395's eligibility-engine work.
Why NUMA topology silently costs you inference throughput across Graviton, Intel, and AMD — thread-to-data alignment, SIMD/AMX bandwidth pressure, host-side effects on KV cache offload.

The design of NKI, the Python-embedded DSL for Trainium's memory hierarchy and compute engines, dissecting production FlashAttention and MoE-routing kernels. Go if you want to write kernels, not just call them.
The evaluator is the algorithm: evolving state of the art for $15. A sharp argument about where progress actually comes from.
How Elastic Fabric Adapter carries the largest AI workloads on AWS. The networking half of why your multi-node training run is slow.
Storage architecture as an AI performance lever rather than an afterthought. Complements AIM347.
Open-source agent observability and evals with AgentCore and Langfuse. Sponsored, but Langfuse is a real option if you want to avoid lock-in.
Deploying a real-time video world model on Trainium using Neuron agentic skills that automate compilation, profiling, and kernel selection.
Turning a coding agent into an always-on dev team with AgentCore.
Trainium3 microarchitecture: NeuronCore changes, hardware quantization, softmax acceleration, MoE optimizations, and UltraServer scaling to 144 chips. Go if you evaluate silicon.
World model serving with torch.compile graph fusion and NKI custom kernels for attention. Pairs naturally with INV511.
Workshop on frontier-model inference economics on Trainium with the Neuron stack and open-source frameworks. Overlaps AIM311 — pick one.
Anthropic models on AWS: what is available and how to deploy it. Efficient orientation if Claude is in your stack.
Where EC2 G7e/G7 beats the P-family for prefill, FP4 decode, and pipeline-parallel training, with a TCO comparison. Practical cost-control material.
Serverless model customization APIs across SFT, DPO, RLVR, RLAIF, and multi-turn RL with no GPUs to manage. The low-friction path when procurement is the bottleneck.
The Kubernetes-flavored version of AIM403: HyperPod on EKS with checkpointless recovery, then inference on the same cluster. Choose based on whether your platform is EKS.
Platform-level what's-new across SageMaker: lakehouse, catalog, governance, dev experience. Efficient way to catch launches without sitting through a keynote.
Agent retrieval specifically on OpenSearch Service. Narrower than ANT311; skip if you take that one.
Building a managed context layer from semantic data with AWS Context. New primitive worth understanding early.
A production-readiness framework for agents: evaluate, disclose, safeguard. Useful checklist material for a review board.
Crash prediction models combining HPC and AI — a concrete simulation-plus-ML pattern.
Genomics HPC pipeline workshop. Take it as a template for any scientific batch pipeline, not just bioinformatics.
Model customization and serving on EKS at high GPU utilization, including hybrid nodes spanning cloud and on-premises GPUs.
How Kiro improves across sessions. Interesting for how they built the learning loop, not just for using the tool.
Kiro Crew internals: orchestration, memory, and safe autonomy. Architecture-level view of a multi-agent coding system.
Strategic framing on AI/HPC for defense and national security. Low technical density — go if you need material for leadership conversations.
Georgia DCS contact center modernization on Amazon Connect. Useful mostly for the stakeholder-alignment and use-case-prioritization lessons.
Measuring emergent risks in frontier models. Research-flavored, useful if you advise on model selection policy.
Cross-partition connectivity between commercial, GovCloud, and Sovereign Cloud: VPN, Direct Connect, DNS, and compliance-boundary enforcement. Niche, but nobody else covers it.
Iceberg data lakes on S3 Tables. The managed-table-maintenance question, answered.
Storage throughput and IOPS tuning for HPC. Pairs with AIM347's Lustre material.
AI-driven serverless development with Kiro. Take it if serverless is your default application shape.
Hands-on lab: fine-tune for valid tool-call output and consistent persona, then ground it with Bedrock RAG. Good if you want the fine-tune-vs-RAG tradeoff in your hands.
Bootcamp on the AI-Driven Development Lifecycle. Longer format — only worth it if you are trying to change how a whole team works.
